title: HTTP
summary: The protocol almost all web backends are built on.

cards.question: What does it mean for an HTTP method to be idempotent?
cards.answer: Repeating the same request leaves the server in the same final state. GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST is not.

cards.question: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
cards.answer: PUT replaces the whole resource; PATCH applies a partial change. PUT is idempotent by definition, PATCH depends on its implementation.

cards.question: What problem does HTTP/2 solve compared to HTTP/1.1?
cards.answer: Stream multiplexing over a single TCP connection, removing HTTP-level head-of-line blocking, and header compression with HPACK. TCP-level blocking remains; HTTP/3 (QUIC) fixes it.
